  107|         of type ``Keyword`` the comparison is case-insensitive. For
  108|         convenience, a single value can be given passed as a string.
  109|         If *regex* is ``True``, the given values are treated as regular
  110|         expressions. Partial matches are allowed. Defaults to ``False``.
  111|         """
  112|         type_matched = self.ttype is ttype
  113|         if not type_matched or values is None:
  114|             return type_matched
  115| 
  116|         if isinstance(values, str):
  117|             values = (values,)
  118| 
  119|         if regex:
  120|             # TODO: Add test for regex with is_keyword = false
  121|             flag = re.IGNORECASE if self.is_keyword else 0
  122|             values = (re.compile(v, flag) for v in values)
  123| 
  124|             return any(pattern.search(self.normalized) for pattern in values)
  125| 
  126|         if self.is_keyword:
  127|             values = (v.upper() for v in values)
  128| 
  129|         return self.normalized in values

  131|     def within(self, group_cls):
  132|         """Returns ``True`` if this token is within *group_cls*.

  134|         Use this method for example to check if an identifier is within
  135|         a function: ``t.within(sql.Function)``.

  137|         parent = self.parent
  138|         while parent:
  139|             if isinstance(parent, group_cls):
  140|                 return True
  141|             parent = parent.parent
  142|         return False

  150|         parent = self.parent
  151|         while parent:
  152|             if parent == other:
  153|                 return True
  154|             parent = parent.parent

  191|         token_count = len(self.tokens)
  192|         for idx, token in enumerate(self.tokens):
  193|             cls = token._get_repr_name()
  194|             value = token._get_repr_value()
  195| 
  196|             last = idx == (token_count - 1)
  197|             pre = '`- ' if last else '|- '
  198| 
  199|             q = '"' if value.startswith("'") and value.endswith("'") else "'"
  200|             print(f"{_pre}{pre}{idx} {cls} {q}{value}{q}", file=f)
  201| 
  202|             if token.is_group and (max_depth is None or depth < max_depth):
  203|                 parent_pre = '   ' if last else '|  '
  204|                 token._pprint_tree(max_depth, depth + 1, f, _pre + parent_pre)

  235|     def _token_matching(self, funcs, start=0, end=None, reverse=False):

  240|         if not isinstance(funcs, (list, tuple)):
  241|             funcs = (funcs,)
  242| 
  243|         if reverse:
  244|             assert end is None
  245|             indexes = range(start - 2, -1, -1)
  246|         else:
  247|             if end is None:
  248|                 end = len(self.tokens)
  249|             indexes = range(start, end)
  250|         for idx in indexes:

  252|             for func in funcs:

  288|         If *skip_cm* is ``True`` comments are ignored.

  294|     def token_next(self, idx, skip_ws=True, skip_cm=False, _reverse=False):

  297|         If *skip_ws* is ``True`` (the default) whitespace tokens are ignored.
  298|         If *skip_cm* is ``True`` comments are ignored.

  303|         idx += 1  # alot of code usage current pre-compensates for this

  305|         def matcher(tk):

  315|     def group_tokens(self, grp_cls, start, end, include_end=True,
  316|                      extend=False):

  318|         start_idx = start
  319|         start = self.tokens[start_idx]
  320| 
  321|         end_idx = end + include_end
  322| 
  323|         # will be needed later for new group_clauses
  324|         # while skip_ws and tokens and tokens[-1].is_whitespace:
  325|         #     tokens = tokens[:-1]
  326| 
  327|         if extend and isinstance(start, grp_cls):
  328|             subtokens = self.tokens[start_idx + 1:end_idx]
  329| 
  330|             grp = start
  331|             grp.tokens.extend(subtokens)
  332|             del self.tokens[start_idx + 1:end_idx]
  333|             grp.value += ''.join(token.value for token in subtokens)
  334|         else:
  335|             subtokens = self.tokens[start_idx:end_idx]
  336|             grp = grp_cls(subtokens)
  337|             self.tokens[start_idx:end_idx] = [grp]

  411| class Statement(TokenList):
  412|     """Represents a SQL statement."""

  414|     def get_type(self):
  415|         """Returns the type of a statement.
  416| 
  417|         The returned value is a string holding an upper-cased reprint of
  418|         the first DML or DDL keyword. If the first token in this group
  419|         isn't a DML or DDL keyword "UNKNOWN" is returned.
  420| 
  421|         Whitespaces and comments at the beginning of the statement
  422|         are ignored.
  423|         """
  424|         token = self.token_first(skip_cm=True)
  425|         if token is None:
  426|             # An "empty" statement that either has not tokens at all
  427|             # or only whitespace tokens.
  428|             return 'UNKNOWN'
  429| 
  430|         elif token.ttype in (T.Keyword.DML, T.Keyword.DDL):
  431|             return token.normalized
  432| 
  433|         elif token.ttype == T.Keyword.CTE:
  434|             # The WITH keyword should be followed by either an Identifier or
  435|             # an IdentifierList containing the CTE definitions;  the actual
  436|             # DML keyword (e.g. SELECT, INSERT) will follow next.
  437|             tidx = self.token_index(token)
  438|             while tidx is not None:
  439|                 tidx, token = self.token_next(tidx, skip_ws=True)
  440|                 if isinstance(token, (Identifier, IdentifierList)):
  441|                     tidx, token = self.token_next(tidx, skip_ws=True)
  442| 
  443|                     if token is not None \
  444|                             and token.ttype == T.Keyword.DML:
  445|                         return token.normalized
  446| 
  447|         # Hmm, probably invalid syntax, so return unknown.
  448|         return 'UNKNOWN'

  581|     def get_cases(self, skip_ws=False):
  582|         """Returns a list of 2-tuples (condition, value).
  583| 
  584|         If an ELSE exists condition is None.
  585|         """
  586|         CONDITION = 1
  587|         VALUE = 2
  588| 
  589|         ret = []
  590|         mode = CONDITION
  591| 
  592|         for token in self.tokens:
  593|             # Set mode from the current statement
  594|             if token.match(T.Keyword, 'CASE') or (skip_ws and token.ttype in T.Whitespace):
  595|                 continue
  596| 
  597|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'WHEN'):
  598|                 ret.append(([], []))
  599|                 mode = CONDITION
  600| 
  601|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'THEN'):
  602|                 mode = VALUE
  603| 
  604|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'ELSE'):
  605|                 ret.append((None, []))
  606|                 mode = VALUE
  607| 
  608|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'END'):
  609|                 mode = None
  610| 
  611|             # First condition without preceding WHEN
  612|             if mode and not ret:
  613|                 ret.append(([], []))
  614| 
  615|             # Append token depending of the current mode
  616|             if mode == CONDITION:
  617|                 ret[-1][0].append(token)
  618| 
  619|             elif mode == VALUE:
  620|                 ret[-1][1].append(token)
  621| 
  622|         # Return cases list
  623|         return ret

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text

function.name: write_file

   42| class Token:
   43|     """Base class for all other classes in this module.
   44| 
   45|     It represents a single token and has two instance attributes:
   46|     ``value`` is the unchanged value of the token and ``ttype`` is
   47|     the type of the token.
   48|     """
   49| 
   50|     __slots__ = (
   51|         'is_group',
   52|         'is_keyword',
   53|         'is_newline',
   54|         'is_whitespace',
   55|         'normalized',
   56|         'parent',
   57|         'ttype',
   58|         'value',
   59|     )
   60| 
   61|     def __init__(self, ttype, value):
   62|         value = str(value)
   63|         self.value = value
   64|         self.ttype = ttype
   65|         self.parent = None
   66|         self.is_group = False
   67|         self.is_keyword = ttype in T.Keyword
   68|         self.is_whitespace = self.ttype in T.Whitespace
   69|         self.is_newline = self.ttype in T.Newline
   70|         self.normalized = value.upper() if self.is_keyword else value
   71| 
   72|     def __str__(self):
   73|         return self.value
   74| 
   75|     # Pending tokenlist __len__ bug fix
   76|     # def __len__(self):
   77|     #     return len(self.value)

   79|     def __repr__(self):
   80|         cls = self._get_repr_name()
   81|         value = self._get_repr_value()
   82| 
   83|         q = '"' if value.startswith("'") and value.endswith("'") else "'"
   84|         return "<{cls} {q}{value}{q} at 0x{id:2X}>".format(
   85|             id=id(self), **locals())
   86| 
   87|     def _get_repr_name(self):
   88|         return str(self.ttype).split('.')[-1]
   89| 
   90|     def _get_repr_value(self):
   91|         raw = str(self)
   92|         if len(raw) > 7:
   93|             raw = raw[:6] + '...'
   94|         return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', raw)

   96|     def flatten(self):

  100|     def match(self, ttype, values, regex=False):
  101|         """Checks whether the token matches the given arguments.
  102| 
  103|         *ttype* is a token type as defined in `sqlparse.tokens`. If it does
  104|         not match, ``False`` is returned.
  105|         *values* is a list of possible values for this token. For match to be
  106|         considered valid, the token value needs to be in this list. For tokens
  107|         of type ``Keyword`` the comparison is case-insensitive. For
  108|         convenience, a single value can be given passed as a string.
  109|         If *regex* is ``True``, the given values are treated as regular
  110|         expressions. Partial matches are allowed. Defaults to ``False``.
  111|         """
  112|         type_matched = self.ttype is ttype
  113|         if not type_matched or values is None:
  114|             return type_matched
  115| 
  116|         if isinstance(values, str):
  117|             values = (values,)
  118| 
  119|         if regex:
  120|             # TODO: Add test for regex with is_keyword = false
  121|             flag = re.IGNORECASE if self.is_keyword else 0
  122|             values = (re.compile(v, flag) for v in values)
  123| 
  124|             return any(pattern.search(self.normalized) for pattern in values)
  125| 
  126|         if self.is_keyword:
  127|             values = (v.upper() for v in values)
  128| 
  129|         return self.normalized in values
  130| 
  131|     def within(self, group_cls):
  132|         """Returns ``True`` if this token is within *group_cls*.
  133| 
  134|         Use this method for example to check if an identifier is within
  135|         a function: ``t.within(sql.Function)``.
  136|         """
  137|         parent = self.parent
  138|         while parent:
  139|             if isinstance(parent, group_cls):
  140|                 return True
  141|             parent = parent.parent
  142|         return False
  143| 
  144|     def is_child_of(self, other):
  145|         """Returns ``True`` if this token is a direct child of *other*."""
  146|         return self.parent == other
  147| 
  148|     def has_ancestor(self, other):
  149|         """Returns ``True`` if *other* is in this tokens ancestry."""
  150|         parent = self.parent
  151|         while parent:
  152|             if parent == other:
  153|                 return True
  154|             parent = parent.parent
  155|         return False

  189|     def _pprint_tree(self, max_depth=None, depth=0, f=None, _pre=''):
  190|         """Pretty-print the object tree."""
  191|         token_count = len(self.tokens)
  192|         for idx, token in enumerate(self.tokens):
  193|             cls = token._get_repr_name()
  194|             value = token._get_repr_value()
  195| 
  196|             last = idx == (token_count - 1)
  197|             pre = '`- ' if last else '|- '
  198| 
  199|             q = '"' if value.startswith("'") and value.endswith("'") else "'"
  200|             print(f"{_pre}{pre}{idx} {cls} {q}{value}{q}", file=f)
  201| 
  202|             if token.is_group and (max_depth is None or depth < max_depth):
  203|                 parent_pre = '   ' if last else '|  '
  204|                 token._pprint_tree(max_depth, depth + 1, f, _pre + parent_pre)

  209|         for token in self.flatten():

  211|             if idx <= offset < end:

  213|             idx = end

  215|     def flatten(self):

  219|         """
  220|         for token in self.tokens:
  221|             if token.is_group:

  235|     def _token_matching(self, funcs, start=0, end=None, reverse=False):
  236|         """next token that match functions"""
  237|         if start is None:
  238|             return None
  239| 
  240|         if not isinstance(funcs, (list, tuple)):
  241|             funcs = (funcs,)
  242| 
  243|         if reverse:
  244|             assert end is None
  245|             indexes = range(start - 2, -1, -1)
  246|         else:
  247|             if end is None:
  248|                 end = len(self.tokens)
  249|             indexes = range(start, end)
  250|         for idx in indexes:
  251|             token = self.tokens[idx]
  252|             for func in funcs:
  253|                 if func(token):
  254|                     return idx, token
  255|         return None, None

  257|     def token_first(self, skip_ws=True, skip_cm=False):

  260|         If *skip_ws* is ``True`` (the default), whitespace

  264|         ignored too.

  266|         # this on is inconsistent, using Comment instead of T.Comment...
  267|         def matcher(tk):

  269|                         or (skip_cm and imt(tk, t=T.Comment, i=Comment)))

  272|     def token_next_by(self, i=None, m=None, t=None, idx=-1, end=None):

  284|     def token_prev(self, idx, skip_ws=True, skip_cm=False):

  287|         If *skip_ws* is ``True`` (the default) whitespace tokens are ignored.
  288|         If *skip_cm* is ``True`` comments are ignored.

  293|     # TODO: May need to re-add default value to idx

  298|         If *skip_cm* is ``True`` comments are ignored.
  299|         ``None`` is returned if there's no next token.

  414|     def get_type(self):
  415|         """Returns the type of a statement.
  416| 
  417|         The returned value is a string holding an upper-cased reprint of
  418|         the first DML or DDL keyword. If the first token in this group
  419|         isn't a DML or DDL keyword "UNKNOWN" is returned.
  420| 
  421|         Whitespaces and comments at the beginning of the statement
  422|         are ignored.
  423|         """
  424|         token = self.token_first(skip_cm=True)
  425|         if token is None:
  426|             # An "empty" statement that either has not tokens at all
  427|             # or only whitespace tokens.
  428|             return 'UNKNOWN'
  429| 
  430|         elif token.ttype in (T.Keyword.DML, T.Keyword.DDL):
  431|             return token.normalized
  432| 
  433|         elif token.ttype == T.Keyword.CTE:
  434|             # The WITH keyword should be followed by either an Identifier or
  435|             # an IdentifierList containing the CTE definitions;  the actual
  436|             # DML keyword (e.g. SELECT, INSERT) will follow next.
  437|             tidx = self.token_index(token)
  438|             while tidx is not None:
  439|                 tidx, token = self.token_next(tidx, skip_ws=True)
  440|                 if isinstance(token, (Identifier, IdentifierList)):
  441|                     tidx, token = self.token_next(tidx, skip_ws=True)
  442| 
  443|                     if token is not None \
  444|                             and token.ttype == T.Keyword.DML:
  445|                         return token.normalized
  446| 
  447|         # Hmm, probably invalid syntax, so return unknown.
  448|         return 'UNKNOWN'

  582|         """Returns a list of 2-tuples (condition, value).
  583| 
  584|         If an ELSE exists condition is None.
  585|         """
  586|         CONDITION = 1
  587|         VALUE = 2
  588| 
  589|         ret = []
  590|         mode = CONDITION
  591| 
  592|         for token in self.tokens:
  593|             # Set mode from the current statement
  594|             if token.match(T.Keyword, 'CASE') or (skip_ws and token.ttype in T.Whitespace):
  595|                 continue
  596| 
  597|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'WHEN'):
  598|                 ret.append(([], []))
  599|                 mode = CONDITION
  600| 
  601|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'THEN'):
  602|                 mode = VALUE
  603| 
  604|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'ELSE'):
  605|                 ret.append((None, []))
  606|                 mode = VALUE
  607| 
  608|             elif token.match(T.Keyword, 'END'):
  609|                 mode = None
  610| 
  611|             # First condition without preceding WHEN
  612|             if mode and not ret:
  613|                 ret.append(([], []))
  614| 
  615|             # Append token depending of the current mode
  616|             if mode == CONDITION:
  617|                 ret[-1][0].append(token)
  618| 
  619|             elif mode == VALUE:
  620|                 ret[-1][1].append(token)
  621| 
  622|         # Return cases list
  623|         return ret

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

structured_output.content:
The regression was in `group_as()` in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py. The `valid_next` check was inverted: it only allowed grouping an `AS` keyword into an Identifier when the token *after* AS was a DML/DDL/CTE keyword (i.e., only for `CREATE ... AS SELECT` / `WITH x AS (...)` style constructs), which is backwards from the intended logic. This meant plain `<expr> AS <alias>` cases (e.g. `foo(x) AS a`) were NOT grouped into an Identifier, leaving bare `AS` keywords dangling in the token stream. That in turn broke downstream grouping/formatting logic (comment stripping whitespace insertion, reindent's identifier-list indentation for functions, etc.) since those filters rely on `AS` aliases being properly grouped into Identifier nodes.

Fixed by negating the condition: `valid_next` must return `True` when the token following AS is *not* a DML/DDL/CTE keyword (so plain aliasing works), while leaving `CREATE ... AS SELECT`, `WITH x AS (SELECT ...)`, etc. appropriately excluded from being swallowed into the Identifier group (since those are followed by a DML/DDL/CTE statement that should remain separate).

Verified after the fix:
- `foo(x) AS a, bar(y) AS b, baz(z) AS c` now groups into a proper IdentifierList of Identifier(Function AS alias) nodes, and reindent produces correctly aligned single-indent output instead of cascading misindentation.
- Comment stripping (`strip_comments=True`) still preserves whitespace/newlines correctly.
- `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1`, `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 1`, and `WITH x AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM x` still reindent correctly (AS not absorbed into the Identifier before a nested SELECT).
- Simple `SELECT a AS b FROM t` and `INSERT INTO t SELECT 1` remain correct.

No test files were found in the workspace to run directly (glob for test_*.py / *test* returned none), so verification was done via direct behavioral checks against the reported failing scenarios and known-good scenarios to ensure no regressions.

message.content:
The regression was in `group_as()` in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py. The `valid_next` check was inverted: it only allowed grouping an `AS` keyword into an Identifier when the token *after* AS was a DML/DDL/CTE keyword (i.e., only for `CREATE ... AS SELECT` / `WITH x AS (...)` style constructs), which is backwards from the intended logic. This meant plain `<expr> AS <alias>` cases (e.g. `foo(x) AS a`) were NOT grouped into an Identifier, leaving bare `AS` keywords dangling in the token stream. That in turn broke downstream grouping/formatting logic (comment stripping whitespace insertion, reindent's identifier-list indentation for functions, etc.) since those filters rely on `AS` aliases being properly grouped into Identifier nodes.

Fixed by negating the condition: `valid_next` must return `True` when the token following AS is *not* a DML/DDL/CTE keyword (so plain aliasing works), while leaving `CREATE ... AS SELECT`, `WITH x AS (SELECT ...)`, etc. appropriately excluded from being swallowed into the Identifier group (since those are followed by a DML/DDL/CTE statement that should remain separate).

Verified after the fix:
- `foo(x) AS a, bar(y) AS b, baz(z) AS c` now groups into a proper IdentifierList of Identifier(Function AS alias) nodes, and reindent produces correctly aligned single-indent output instead of cascading misindentation.
- Comment stripping (`strip_comments=True`) still preserves whitespace/newlines correctly.
- `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1`, `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT 1`, and `WITH x AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM x` still reindent correctly (AS not absorbed into the Identifier before a nested SELECT).
- Simple `SELECT a AS b FROM t` and `INSERT INTO t SELECT 1` remain correct.

No test files were found in the workspace to run directly (glob for test_*.py / *test* returned none), so verification was done via direct behavioral checks against the reported failing scenarios and known-good scenarios to ensure no regressions.
